own_solution.law: Doppler effect, moving source, stationary observer in still air: f' = f v/(v - v_s)
assumptions: source moves directly toward listener (approach phase)
listener hears the emitted tone; emitted tone 440 Hz unless changed

notes: Base: 440*343/323 = 467.245 Hz. With siren raised to 456 Hz: 456*343/323 = 484.235 Hz. Distance 300 m does not enter the Doppler shift for constant-velocity approach (it only sets when the siren passes, after 15 s); I label it C (it enters arrival-time relations but cancels from the frequency) though K (approach phase) is also defensible. Earlier-run tuning (T62DC, TEE83) is before the switch-on that fixes the stated 440 Hz, so no path to the answer. T8B99 'soon after the tone begins' implicitly assumes the listener's hearing is after the retuning; mild timing ambiguity. Variant sets: T5688/T8B99/TD410/TEE83 all state 16 Hz; TE5DD/T4EE7 both 300 m. TEDCB and T62DC say 'a small amount' with no number; if they are meant as minimal-pair variants of 16 Hz sentences, they differ in the stated value.
